Title: "Independent Verification Memo: WO-01 Pump Module Selection for the Water-Reclamation Transfer Loop"

Executive summary (~700 chars): "This memo independently verifies the analyst's report against the trusted table. All four modules pass the written screen: quality 80–97, all at or above 80, and raw defect counts 0–4, all within the ceiling of 5. Measured energy on the shared fixed-duty acceptance run is 12 kWh (P2), 52 (P3), 56 (P1) and 58 (P4). Recomputed gaps of 40, 44 and 46 kWh confirm the analyst's arithmetic; the minimum is unique, so the tie-break rule is not engaged. The policy selects the lowest-energy qualifying package, which is P2; my independent ballot is P2. I find no factual errors in the delivered report. Three questions remain open — whether zero defects should carry weight beyond the ceiling, whether P1's four defects are stable, and whether quality indices are independently measured — none affects the written outcome."

Sections:

1. "Independent Eligibility Recomputation" (~600 chars): From the trusted table alone: P1 quality 84, defects 4; P2 97/1; P3 80/3; P4 81/0. Threshold quality ≥80 and defects ≤5. Every candidate passes: the quality minimum is met exactly by P3 and with a 17-point margin by P2; the defect ceiling is cleared by 1, 4, 2 and 5 counts respectively. P1's margin of one defect is a robustness caveat: a single retest could disqualify it, though today's record is unaffected. All four modules therefore qualify; reject_all is not applicable.

2. "Verified Energy Ranking and Gap Arithmetic" (~640): Ranking: 12, 52, 56, 58. I recomputed gaps: 52−12=40; 56−12=44; 58−12=46, matching A. Ratios: P3 ≈4.33×, P1 ≈4.67×, P4 ≈4.83× the leader's consumption. Since BASIS states every module serves the same fixed flow and head on one test basis, these differences reflect module efficiency, not duty or measurement artifacts — a premise I verified in the work order, not from A. The minimum is unique at 12 kWh, so the lowest-ID tie-break is unnecessary. No cost, delivery or maintenance data exists in the supplied facts, so none enters the ranking.

3. "Facts, Assumptions and Open Questions": Facts are limited to the trusted table and the shared-basis statement. Unverified: cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability; explicitly excluded. Open questions carried from the report, which I judge legitimate but non-binding: (i) whether defect counts should carry weight beyond the pass/fail ceiling — P4's zero-defect record is the only such signal; (ii) whether P1's 4-defect count is stable against retest; (iii) whether the quality indices are independently measured. The written policy is unambiguous: energy is the sole optimizer among qualifiers, so none of these changes the selection under current rules.

4. "Verification Verdict and Ballot Basis": I checked the delivered report's screening, gap sums, and recommendation against the sources and found no factual errors or unsupported claims; the flagged open questions are correctly labeled as open. My ballot: P2, because it qualifies (quality 97, 1 defect) and posts the unique minimum energy of 12 kWh under the written selection rule. I make this judgment independently of the analyst; the arithmetic is trivially re-derivable from the table. Handover note for C: record the defect-margin column and the three open questions for the next analyst.

Recommendation: P2. Rationale: "P2 qualifies (quality 97, one defect) and posts the unique minimum measured energy of 12 kWh on the shared fixed-duty run, 40–46 kWh ahead of every rival; the written policy selects the lowest-energy qualifying package. P4's zero-defect record is logged as an open secondary signal only." (~250 chars, fine.)

Figure caption: "Verification diagram: recomputed energy ranking on the shared acceptance run with eligibility margins; P2 leads at 12 kWh with verified gaps of 40, 44 and 46 kWh."

Word count estimate: exec ~130 words, sections ~110 each = 440, plus title/caption/rec ~50 → ~620. Within range. Byte count: ~3700 bytes, fine.

Style: serif, single_column, accent #1B7A8C.

One publish_document call.
